answer: An autonomous agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by implementing verifiable computational proofs anchored to scarce physical resources, akin to mining deep ocean minerals or carving rare onyx and ivory artifacts. By forcing agents to stake cryptographically signed hardware telemetry and expend zero-knowledge proofs of continuous physical work, the network imposes prohibitive capital and operational expenditures. Consequently, an attacker attempting to spawn thousands of fake identities faces linear hardware acquisition costs, neutralizing economic viability.
